picks.reasoning: Strip away the banners and the reigning-champion hype and you're left with the players, and T1's are the stronger group, the same gap that has shown up in every LCK-versus-CBLOL meeting this year. LOS's comeback habit is real, but it's a habit built against weaker opposition, and I won't mistake a scrappy 2025 CBLOL squad's stubbornness for a better lineup.

LOS owns the early map: they take towers and set the pace before 15, and that's the part of this matchup I trust most. But LCK-versus-CBLOL is the biggest gap on the board, and LOS's results against other regions are thin, so I won't let one good tempo stretch overrule that. T1 can lose the first ten minutes and still win the fight that decides the game.

Draft is where this series gets decided, and T1's mid-lane depth on Anivia, Orianna and Akali gives them more ways to bend a Fearless board than LOS's Ryze-heavy setup. LOS's hot streak is real, but the gap between these two regions is wide enough that I'm not betting against the LCK side on a single game.

LOS's 9-of-10 run and slightly better 15-minute gold numbers are real, but the international evidence is what matters here, and it points to LCK: CBLOL is 0-3 against them this year, and LCK's 15-7 international record dwarfs CBLOL's 4-7. T1 has also closed out games late in this stretch, and a Worlds champion in a best-of-1 is the safer read.

Rosters decide these games more than the badge on the jersey, and T1's last stretch looks like a group that's lost its rhythm, with the 9-11 run and a lot of late-game wobbling in their recent nights. But LOS are a team that keeps finding a way back and then has to hold their nerve in a room full of LCK pressure, and that's a hard thing to do on this stage. I'll still back T1, because the region gap is too big to ignore and their experience in these moments usually shows up when it matters.
